title: Soto Ayam
description: Turmeric chicken soup with rice cakes, beansprouts and a squeeze of lime.
why_it_fits: A warm, turmeric-scented broth slows you down, and lean chicken keeps you steady without feeling heavy.
image_credit: Gunawan Kartapranata / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic and ginger into a rough paste.
Fry the paste in oil with turmeric and bruised lemongrass for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the stock and chicken, then simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it, and season the broth with salt.
Divide rice cakes and blanched beansprouts between bowls, top with chicken and ladle over the hot broth.
Finish with fried shallots and a squeeze of lime.

title: Teochew Fish Porridge
description: Light rice porridge with tender fish slices, ginger and spring onion.
why_it_fits: Soft, plain and easy to digest — a bowl that asks nothing of you on a day that already asks a lot.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it in the stock for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and soupy.
Slice the fish thinly and toss with half the soy sauce and the white pepper.
Cut the ginger into fine matchsticks and add to the porridge.
Slide in the fish slices and cook gently for 3 minutes until just opaque.
Season with the remaining soy sauce, then top with spring onion and a few drops of sesame oil.

title: Steamed Egg with Minced Chicken
description: Silky savoury egg custard over minced chicken, served with warm rice.
why_it_fits: Silky, gentle and protein-rich; simple comfort food that settles rather than stimulates.
steps: Cook the rice.
Season the minced chicken with half the soy sauce and spread it over the base of a shallow heatproof dish.
Beat the eggs gently with the stock (warm, not hot) and strain over the chicken.
Cover the dish with a plate and steam over low heat for 12-15 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Drizzle with the remaining soy sauce and sesame oil, scatter over spring onion, and serve with the rice.

title: Sayur Lodeh with Rice
description: Vegetables, tofu and tempeh simmered in a gentle coconut gravy.
why_it_fits: A mild coconut gravy full of vegetables — nourishing, unhurried and calming to cook.
steps: Cook the rice.
Pound or blend the shallots and garlic, then fry in oil with turmeric and bruised lemongrass until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk plus 200 ml water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the carrot and long beans and cook for 5 minutes, then add the cabbage, cubed tofu and tempeh.
Simmer for another 8-10 minutes until the vegetables are tender, and season with salt.
Serve ladled over the rice.

title: Sliced Fish Bee Hoon Soup
description: Clear, gingery fish soup with rice vermicelli and leafy greens.
why_it_fits: Light protein and a gingery broth lift your energy without the heaviness that makes a slump worse.
image_credit: Bonkers The Clown / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
steps: Soak the vermicelli in hot water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Bring the stock to a simmer with sliced ginger and tomato wedges for 5 minutes.
Add the sliced fish and chye sim and cook for 3 minutes until the fish turns opaque.
Stir in the evaporated milk, soy sauce and sesame oil.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the soup and top with fried shallots.

title: Black Pepper Beef Rice Bowl
description: Quick-seared beef and capsicum in a punchy black pepper sauce over rice.
why_it_fits: Iron-rich beef and a peppery kick wake you up, with rice for steady fuel.
image_credit: Alpha from Melbourne, Australia / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0
steps: Cook the rice.
Slice the beef thinly against the grain and toss with soy sauce and cornflour.
Sear the beef in hot oil for 1 minute per side, then set aside.
Stir-fry the onion, garlic and capsicum for 2 minutes until just softened.
Return the beef with the oyster sauce, coarsely cracked black pepper and a splash of water, and toss for 1 minute.
Serve straight over the rice.

title: Nasi Goreng Kampung
description: Village-style fried rice with anchovies, kangkung, chilli and a fried egg.
why_it_fits: Bold sambal heat, crunchy anchovies and an egg on top — a plate with enough punch to shake off a slow day.
steps: Fry the anchovies in oil until crisp, then lift out and set aside.
Pound the shallots, garlic and chilli, and fry the paste in the same oil with the sambal belacan until fragrant.
Add the rice and soy sauce and toss over high heat for 3 minutes.
Stir through the kangkung until just wilted.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in a separate pan.
Serve the rice topped with an egg and the crispy anchovies.

title: Thai Basil Chicken with Fried Egg
description: Fiery minced chicken stir-fry with holy basil, rice and a crispy egg.
why_it_fits: Chilli, basil and plenty of protein, ready in 15 minutes when you have little energy to cook.
steps: Cook the rice.
Roughly chop the garlic and chilli and fry in hot oil for 30 seconds.
Add the minced chicken and break it up, cooking for 4 minutes until browned.
Add the chopped long beans, oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar, and toss for 2 minutes.
Take off the heat and fold through the basil until wilted.
Fry the eggs until the edges are crisp and serve everything over rice.

title: Tomato Egg Rice Bowl
description: Soft scrambled eggs in a sweet-tangy tomato sauce over steamed rice.
why_it_fits: Sweet, soft and familiar — the kind of home cooking that feels like being looked after.
image_credit: Wikimedia Commons contributor / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
steps: Cook the rice.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and scramble in hot oil until just set, then tip out.
Fry the garlic, then add tomato wedges and cook for 3 minutes until they start to collapse.
Stir in the ketchup, sugar, soy sauce and 3 tbsp water and simmer for 2 minutes.
Return the eggs and fold gently through the sauce.
Spoon over the rice and top with spring onion.

title: Chicken Macaroni Soup
description: The kopitiam classic: tender macaroni and shredded chicken in clear broth.
why_it_fits: A kopitiam classic: warm, mild broth and soft pasta for a gentle lift on a low day.
steps: Bring the stock to a simmer with the smashed garlic.
Add the chicken breast and poach gently for 12 minutes, then lift out and shred.
Add the diced carrot and macaroni to the broth and cook for 8 minutes until tender.
Return the chicken and season with salt and white pepper.
Serve topped with fried shallots and spring onion.

title: Ayam Masak Merah with Rice
description: Chicken braised in a rich, mildly spicy tomato-chilli gravy.
why_it_fits: Rich, sweet-spicy gravy over rice is deep comfort food that meets a heavy mood halfway.
steps: Cook the rice.
Rub the chicken with salt and pan-fry in oil until golden on both sides, then set aside.
Blend the onion, garlic and ginger and fry the paste with the cinnamon and star anise for 3 minutes.
Add the chilli paste and cook until the oil separates, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato puree, ketchup, sugar, tomato wedges and 150 ml water.
Return the chicken and simmer for 15 minutes until the gravy is thick and glossy, then serve with rice.

title: Mee Rebus
description: Yellow noodles in a thick, sweet-savoury sweet potato gravy with egg and lime.
why_it_fits: A thick, sweet-savoury gravy and all the toppings make this a properly comforting bowl.
steps: Boil the sweet potato until soft, then mash smooth. Hard-boil the eggs.
Blend the shallots and garlic and fry in oil with the curry powder and soybean paste until fragrant.
Add the beef mince and brown it, then pour in the stock.
Whisk in the mashed sweet potato and simmer for 10 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Blanch the noodles and beansprouts and divide between bowls.
Ladle over the gravy and top with halved egg, fried tofu cubes, sliced green chilli and lime.

title: Roti John
description: Pan-toasted baguette with a spiced egg and minced chicken omelette.
why_it_fits: Fun, messy and made for sharing — a good mood deserves something a little playful.
image_credit: stef yau from Seattle, USA / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0
steps: Fry the diced onion, garlic and minced chicken with the curry powder until cooked, then cool slightly.
Beat the eggs and stir in the chicken mixture with a pinch of salt.
Split the baguette lengthways without cutting all the way through.
Melt the butter in a wide pan, pour in the egg mixture and press the open baguette cut-side down onto it.
Cook for 3 minutes until set, then flip and toast the crust for 1 minute.
Fill with chilli sauce, mayonnaise and sliced cucumber, then slice and serve.

title: Ayam Penyet
description: Crispy smashed fried chicken with fiery sambal, tofu, tempeh and rice.
why_it_fits: Crispy chicken and fiery sambal: a lively plate that matches high spirits.
image_credit: D.W. Fisher-Freberg / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
steps: Cook the rice.
Simmer the chicken for 15 minutes in just enough water with turmeric, coriander, crushed garlic and salt.
Drain and pat dry, then shallow-fry until deep golden and crisp. Fry the tofu and tempeh in the same oil.
Fry the chilli, shallots and tomato until soft, then pound with salt and lime juice into a coarse sambal.
Lightly smash the chicken with a pestle so it cracks open.
Serve with the sambal, tofu, tempeh, cucumber and rice.

title: Halal Prawn Hokkien Mee
description: Wok-braised yellow noodles and bee hoon in prawn stock, with squid and lime.
why_it_fits: A hawker favourite worth savouring, with bright lime and seafood to keep the mood up.
steps: Peel the prawns and simmer the shells and heads in the stock for 10 minutes, then strain.
Fry the garlic in hot oil, scramble in the eggs, then add both noodles and toss over high heat.
Pour in the prawn stock with the fish sauce and soy sauce, cover and braise for 4 minutes.
Add the prawns and sliced squid and cook for 3 minutes until just done.
Toss through the beansprouts and chives until the noodles are saucy but not soupy.
Serve with sambal and a wedge of lime.

title: Japchae with Beef
description: Glossy sweet potato glass noodles with beef and colourful vegetables.
why_it_fits: Colourful, glossy and celebratory — a dish that looks as upbeat as you feel.
image_credit: Wikimedia Commons contributor / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0
steps: Boil the glass noodles for 6 minutes, rinse under cold water and snip into shorter lengths.
Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and minced garlic into a sauce.
Slice the beef thinly and marinate in 1 tbsp of the sauce.
Stir-fry the onion, carrot, capsicum and mushrooms in oil for 3 minutes, then set aside.
Sear the beef for 2 minutes, add the spinach to wilt, then return the vegetables.
Add the noodles and remaining sauce, toss until glossy and finish with sesame seeds.

title: Tofu & Spinach Miso Soup with Rice
description: A gentle bowl of miso broth, silken tofu and greens with steamed rice.
why_it_fits: A warm, quiet bowl with magnesium-rich tofu and greens gives restless energy somewhere soft to land.
steps: Cook the rice.
Bring 700 ml water to a gentle simmer with the sliced mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Add the wakame and cubed tofu and warm through for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and dissolve the miso in a ladle of the broth before stirring it back in.
Stir in the spinach until just wilted.
Top with spring onion and serve alongside the rice.

title: Steamed Fish with Ginger & Spring Onion
description: Delicate steamed fish dressed with ginger, soy and hot oil.
why_it_fits: Clean, delicate flavours and gentle steaming make a calm meal with nothing to rush.
steps: Cook the rice.
Lay the fish on a plate over half the ginger slices and steam for 8-10 minutes until it flakes easily.
Blanch the chye sim for 1 minute and drain.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil with 1 tbsp hot water.
Pour off the steaming liquid, then top the fish with shredded ginger and spring onion.
Heat the cooking oil until shimmering, pour it over the aromatics, add the sauce and serve with rice and greens.

title: Dhal Curry with Chapati
description: Creamy yellow lentils tempered with cumin and garlic, scooped up with chapati.
why_it_fits: Slow-release lentils and warm spices are grounding, and tearing chapati by hand slows the pace.
image_credit: Wind Hashira / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
steps: Rinse the lentils and simmer with turmeric, diced carrot and 700 ml water for 25 minutes until soft.
Mash lightly with the back of a spoon and season with salt.
Heat the oil and fry the cumin seeds and curry leaves until they crackle.
Add the sliced onion, garlic and ginger and cook until golden, then add the chopped tomato.
Pour this tempering into the lentils and simmer for 3 more minutes.
Warm the chapati in a dry pan and serve alongside.

title: Yong Tau Foo Clear Soup
description: Fish-paste-stuffed tofu and vegetables in a light soybean broth.
why_it_fits: A clear, light broth with simple stuffed vegetables is soothing and easy on a nervous stomach.
steps: Simmer the anchovies in the stock for 10 minutes, then strain.
Cut the tofu into thick triangles and slit each piece, plus the okra, eggplant slices and chilli.
Stuff each pocket with fish paste.
Poach the stuffed pieces in the broth for 6-8 minutes until the fish paste is firm.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water for 5 minutes and blanch the chye sim.
Serve noodles and greens in bowls with the stuffed pieces, broth, soy sauce and fried shallots.

title: Teriyaki Salmon Soba
description: Pan-seared salmon in a honey-soy glaze over chilled soba and edamame.
why_it_fits: Omega-3-rich salmon and slow-release soba give steady fuel for clearer thinking.
steps: Cook the soba for 4 minutes, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Mix the soy sauce, honey and grated ginger into a glaze (no mirin or sake needed).
Sear the salmon skin-side down in oil for 4 minutes, flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Pour in two-thirds of the glaze and let it bubble until sticky.
Toss the soba with the remaining glaze, sesame oil, edamame and cucumber.
Top with the salmon, spring onion and sesame seeds.

title: Sambal Egg & Tempeh Brown Rice Bowl
description: Jammy eggs and crisp tempeh in sambal tumis over nutty brown rice.
why_it_fits: Eggs, tempeh and brown rice give lasting protein and fibre, so your attention doesn't dip an hour later.
steps: Cook the brown rice. Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool and peel.
Slice the tempeh and pan-fry in oil until golden, then set aside.
Fry the sliced onion and garlic, add the chilli paste and cook for 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Stir in the chopped tomato, tamarind, sugar and a splash of water and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the long beans, tempeh and halved eggs and coat in the sambal.
Serve over the brown rice.

title: Assam Pedas Fish
description: Mackerel in a hot-and-sour tamarind gravy with okra and tomato.
why_it_fits: Oily fish for omega-3s and a sharp, sour-spicy gravy that wakes up a foggy head.
image_credit: Elly Suhailee / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
steps: Cook the rice.
Blend the shallots, garlic and ginger and fry in oil with the chilli paste, turmeric and bruised lemongrass.
Cook for 5 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the tamarind mixed with 500 ml water and bring to a simmer.
Add the okra and tomato wedges and cook for 4 minutes.
Slide in the mackerel and simmer for 6-8 minutes until cooked through, season with sugar and salt, and serve with rice.

title: Thunder Tea Rice Bowl
description: Hakka lei cha: brown rice with chopped greens, tofu, peanuts and a herby tea broth.
why_it_fits: Greens, herbs, nuts and brown rice in one bowl — steady energy with nothing to cause a crash.
image_credit: Encik Tekateki / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
steps: Cook the brown rice.
Finely chop the long beans, chye sim and cabbage and stir-fry each briefly with a little garlic and salt.
Dice and pan-fry the tofu until golden, and fry the anchovies until crisp.
Blend the basil, mint, tea leaves, sesame seeds and half the peanuts with 300 ml hot water into a green broth.
Arrange the vegetables, tofu, anchovies and remaining peanuts over the rice.
Serve the tea broth on the side to pour over.

title: Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry
description: Quick-seared beef strips with broccoli in a savoury garlic-ginger sauce.
why_it_fits: Iron-rich beef and quick-release rice carbs combat fatigue and restore alertness fast.
steps: Sear beef strips 2 min per side, set aside.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger, broccoli.
Return beef, add soy sauce, toss.
Serve over rice.

title: Beef Pho
description: Vietnamese beef noodle soup with a fragrant star anise and cinnamon broth.
why_it_fits: The ritual of a slow-sipped aromatic broth gives racing thoughts something steady to follow.
steps: Simmer broth with star anise and cinnamon for 20 minutes.
Pour the hot broth over thinly sliced raw beef and noodles to gently cook the beef through.
Top with basil and beansprouts.

title: Beef Rendang with Steamed Rice
description: Slow-cooked beef in coconut milk and aromatic spices until deeply caramelised.
why_it_fits: Iron-rich beef slow-cooked to tender restores energy that a quick meal can't match.
steps: Blend shallots, lemongrass, and galangal into a paste.
Simmer beef in coconut milk with the paste for 90 minutes until the sauce reduces and the beef is deeply tender.
Serve over rice.

title: Berry & Yogurt Parfait
description: Layered Greek yogurt, mixed berries, and honeyed granola.
why_it_fits: A light, celebratory dish that matches a bright mood without any post-meal slump.
steps: Layer yogurt, berries, and granola in a glass.
Drizzle with honey.

title: Bibimbap with Beef Bulgogi
description: Warm rice bowl with marinated beef bulgogi, sautéed vegetables, and a fried egg.
why_it_fits: The colour, variety, and protein in one mixed bowl gives scattered focus something to gather around.
steps: Marinate and sear beef bulgogi-style.
Sauté each vegetable individually and season lightly.
Assemble everything over rice with a fried egg and a spoon of gochujang.

title: Blueberry Walnut Brain-Boost Bowl
description: Greek yoghurt bowl with blueberries, walnuts, and a drizzle of honey.
why_it_fits: Antioxidant-rich blueberries and omega-3s from walnuts support sharper, clearer thinking.
steps: Spoon yoghurt into a bowl.
Top with blueberries, walnuts, chia seeds, and a drizzle of honey.

title: Butter Chicken with Basmati Rice
description: Creamy tomato-based chicken curry with warm garam masala, served over basmati rice.
why_it_fits: Rich, warm spice and cream deliver the kind of deep comfort that meets a melancholy mood halfway.
steps: Marinate and sear chicken.
Simmer in tomato puree, cream, butter, and garam masala until thick and glossy.
Serve over basmati rice.

title: Chamomile & Almond Overnight Oats
description: Overnight oats soaked in chamomile tea and almond milk, topped with sliced almonds.
why_it_fits: Chamomile and slow-release oats work together to ease nervous energy before it builds.
steps: Mix oats, almond milk, and brewed chamomile.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with sliced almonds and honey.

title: Chamomile Honey Rice Pudding
description: Creamy rice pudding slow-cooked with chamomile-infused milk and honey.
why_it_fits: Chamomile has a mild calming effect and warm milk-based comfort food lowers physical tension.
steps: Steep chamomile in warm milk 5 min, remove bags.
Simmer rice in the milk 25 min, stirring often.
Stir in honey and cinnamon.

title: Chamomile Turkey Meatballs with Brown Rice
description: Gently spiced turkey meatballs simmered in a mild tomato sauce, served over brown rice.
why_it_fits: Lean protein and a slow-simmered sauce make a grounding, unhurried meal that eases a restless mind.
steps: Mix turkey with breadcrumbs and garlic, form meatballs.
Simmer in crushed tomatoes 15 min.
Serve over rice, top with parsley.

title: Chicken Congee
description: Silky rice porridge simmered with shredded chicken, ginger, and scallions.
why_it_fits: A soft, spoonable dish that asks nothing of you — easy to digest when everything feels like a lot.
steps: Simmer rice in stock with ginger for 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and creamy.
Stir in shredded poached chicken.
Top with scallions and a drizzle of sesame oil.

title: Chicken Katsu Curry Rice
description: Crispy breaded chicken cutlet with a mild Japanese curry sauce over rice.
why_it_fits: A satisfying crunch-then-comfort combination gives a distracted mind one clear thing to focus on.
steps: Bread the chicken with panko and pan-fry until golden and crisp.
Simmer curry roux with carrot and onion until thick.
Slice the chicken over rice and ladle the curry sauce on top.

title: Chicken Laksa
description: Creamy coconut curry noodle soup with shredded chicken, tofu puffs, and beansprouts.
why_it_fits: A rich, warming bowl of comfort food that feels like being taken care of on a low day.
steps: Simmer laksa paste with coconut milk and stock.
Add poached shredded chicken and tofu puffs.
Serve over noodles with beansprouts and coriander.

title: Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce
description: Char-grilled marinated chicken skewers with a rich peanut dipping sauce.
why_it_fits: A vibrant, sociable dish that matches and sustains an already bright, energetic mood.
steps: Marinate chicken in turmeric and lemongrass.
Skewer and grill until charred at the edges.
Serve with peanut sauce, rice, and cucumber.

title: Chicken Tikka with Basmati Rice
description: Yogurt-marinated grilled chicken tikka with warm spices over basmati rice.
why_it_fits: Warm spices and a hearty, familiar dish offer grounding comfort on a low day.
steps: Marinate chicken in yogurt and garam masala 20 min.
Grill or pan-sear until cooked through.
Serve over basmati rice with coriander.

title: Dark Chocolate Banana Smoothie Bowl
description: Thick banana smoothie bowl with cacao, topped with berries and granola.
why_it_fits: Cacao supports serotonin production; the ritual of a topped bowl adds a small moment of self-care.
steps: Blend frozen banana, cacao, and almond milk until thick.
Pour into a bowl, top with berries and granola.

title: Golden Turmeric Lentil Soup
description: Warming red lentil soup with turmeric, ginger, and coconut milk.
why_it_fits: Turmeric's curcumin has mood-lifting properties; warm soup provides emotional comfort.
steps: Sauté onion.
Add spices, lentils, stock.
Simmer 20 min.
Stir in coconut milk.

title: Grilled Chicken & Mango Salsa Bowl
description: Charred grilled chicken with a bright mango-lime salsa over jasmine rice.
why_it_fits: A bright, colourful plate matches an upbeat mood and keeps the energy going without weighing you down.
steps: Grill chicken 6 min per side, slice.
Toss diced mango, red onion, lime juice, and cilantro for salsa.
Serve over rice, top with chicken and salsa.

title: Grilled Chicken Fajita Bowl
description: Sizzled chicken and peppers with lime, served over rice with fresh salsa.
why_it_fits: Bright citrus and lean protein match and sustain an already-good mood without weighing you down.
steps: Sear sliced chicken and peppers with lime juice until charred at the edges.
Serve over rice with fresh salsa.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
description: Poached chicken and fragrant chicken-fat rice, served with chilli-ginger and dark soy dipping sauces.
why_it_fits: Lean protein and easy carbs from the rice give a steady, sustained lift out of an energy slump.
image_credit: Wikimedia Commons contributor / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.5
steps: Poach chicken gently in stock with ginger and garlic until just cooked.
Cook rice in the poaching stock.
Slice chicken, serve over rice with cucumber and dipping sauces.

title: Herb-Crusted Baked Cod with Roasted Veg
description: Flaky baked cod with a herb crust, served with roasted seasonal vegetables.
why_it_fits: Lean white fish and B-vitamin-rich vegetables support mental clarity and steady focus.
steps: Press herb-breadcrumb mix onto cod, bake 15 min at 200°C alongside roasted carrots and zucchini.

title: High-Protein Greek Salad Bowl
description: Grilled chicken, chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, and feta on a bed of romaine.
why_it_fits: High protein and iron from chicken + chickpeas combat fatigue and restore energy.
image_credit: Flickr user via Wikimedia Commons / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0
steps: Grill chicken.
Combine all vegetables.
Top with chicken, chickpeas, feta.
Drizzle olive oil.

title: Lemon Herb Pasta with Spinach
description: A light, satisfying pasta with garlic, lemon zest, and wilted spinach.
why_it_fits: Complex carbs boost serotonin; lemon and garlic aromas are calming.
steps: Boil pasta.
Sauté garlic in olive oil, add spinach until wilted.
Toss with pasta, lemon zest, and parmesan.

title: Mee Goreng
description: Spicy stir-fried noodles with chicken, egg, and vegetables in a sweet-savoury sauce.
why_it_fits: The hands-on sizzle of stir-frying gives restless energy something immediate to focus on.
steps: Stir-fry chicken until cooked through.
Push aside and scramble the egg.
Add noodles and dark soy sauce, toss well, then fold in tomato and beansprouts.

title: Miso-Glazed Salmon with Steamed Rice
description: Pan-seared salmon glazed with miso and honey, served over steamed rice.
why_it_fits: Omega-3s in salmon help regulate cortisol; the umami glaze makes it deeply satisfying under stress.
steps: Mix miso and honey, brush onto salmon.
Pan-sear 4 minutes each side.
Serve over rice, top with sliced scallions.

title: Nasi Lemak with Chicken Sambal
description: Fragrant coconut rice with spicy sambal, crispy fried chicken, and all the classic sides.
why_it_fits: The gentle ritual of a full, familiar plate and warming spice can settle a nervous, anxious mind.
steps: Cook rice with coconut milk.
Fry chicken until golden and crisp.
Fry sambal paste with anchovies until fragrant.
Plate rice with chicken, sambal, peanuts, cucumber, and egg.

title: Pad Thai with Prawns
description: Stir-fried rice noodles with prawns, egg, tamarind, and crushed peanuts.
why_it_fits: Bright tamarind and lime keep a good mood light instead of weighing it down.
steps: Soak noodles until pliable.
Stir-fry prawns and egg, add noodles and tamarind sauce, toss well.
Fold in beansprouts, top with peanuts and lime.

title: Salmon & Roasted Sweet Potato Bowl
description: Omega-3 rich salmon fillet with caramelised sweet potato and steamed broccoli.
why_it_fits: Omega-3s in salmon sharpen focus; complex carbs from sweet potato fuel sustained concentration.
steps: Roast sweet potato 25 min.
Pan-fry salmon 4 min each side.
Steam broccoli.
Assemble with soy drizzle.

title: Smashed Avocado & Poached Eggs on Sourdough
description: Creamy avocado, perfectly poached eggs, chilli flakes on thick sourdough.
why_it_fits: Healthy fats sustain your great energy; protein keeps the mood stable all morning.
steps: Toast sourdough.
Smash avocado with lemon.
Poach eggs 3 min.
Assemble, top with chilli flakes.

title: Spiced Chickpea & Sweet Potato Bowl
description: Roasted sweet potato and spiced chickpeas over greens with tahini drizzle.
why_it_fits: Complex carbs and plant protein provide a steady energy release without a sugar crash.
steps: Roast sweet potato and spiced chickpeas 25 min at 200°C.
Serve over spinach, drizzle with tahini.

title: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Power Bowl
description: Roasted sweet potato, black beans, and corn over rice with a lime-yoghurt drizzle.
why_it_fits: Slow-digesting carbs and fibre-rich beans give a steady energy climb instead of a quick crash.
steps: Roast diced sweet potato 20 min at 200°C.
Warm black beans and corn.
Layer over rice, top with yoghurt and lime juice.

title: Turmeric Chicken & Quinoa Power Bowl
description: Turmeric-spiced chicken over quinoa with roasted vegetables and a lemon-tahini drizzle.
why_it_fits: Turmeric and complex carbs from quinoa support sustained mental clarity through the afternoon.
steps: Season chicken with turmeric, pan-sear until cooked.
Serve over quinoa with roasted broccoli and a tahini drizzle.

title: Turmeric Ginger Chicken Soup
description: A warming, golden chicken soup with turmeric, ginger, and soft noodles.
why_it_fits: Turmeric and ginger calm inflammation while a warm broth soothes a racing mind.
steps: Simmer chicken in stock with ginger and turmeric 15 min, shred.
Add carrot and noodles, cook 5 more minutes.

title: Walnut & Berry Overnight Oats
description: Creamy oats soaked overnight, topped with mixed berries and walnuts.
why_it_fits: Magnesium-rich walnuts and slow-release oats reduce cortisol and ease nervous tension.
steps: Mix oats, milk, chia, honey.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with berries and walnuts.

title: Warm Cinnamon Apple Crumble Oats
description: Stovetop oats folded with cinnamon-stewed apple and a crunchy oat topping.
why_it_fits: A warm, spiced comfort bowl gives a small ritual of self-care and a gentle serotonin lift from the carbs.
steps: Simmer oats in milk 5 min.
Sauté diced apple with cinnamon and honey until soft, fold through.
Top with crushed walnuts.

title: Warm Ginger Beef Noodle Soup
description: Comforting broth with tender beef, rice noodles, and fresh ginger.
why_it_fits: A warm, slow-sipped broth gives restless energy something steady to settle into.
steps: Simmer broth with ginger 10 min.
Add beef and bok choy, cook through.
Serve over rice noodles.

title: Baked Mac and Cheese with Crispy Top
description: Creamy three-cheese macaroni baked until the top turns golden and crisp.
why_it_fits: The most classic comfort food there is — a slow bake gives you time to sit with how you feel before the reward arrives.
steps: Make a cheese sauce with butter, milk, and cheeses.
Toss with cooked macaroni, top with breadcrumbs, and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes until golden.

title: Beef Short Rib Ragu over Pappardelle
description: Beef short ribs simmered for hours into a rich tomato ragu, tossed with wide pappardelle noodles.
why_it_fits: Deeply savoury, iron-rich beef slow-cooked to tenderness gives sustained energy without needing to lift a finger while it cooks.
steps: Sear short ribs, then simmer with tomatoes, carrot, and celery for 2.5 hours until the meat shreds easily.
Toss through cooked pappardelle, top with parmesan.

title: Chamomile-Braised Chicken Thighs with Root Vegetables
description: Chicken thighs braised in chamomile-infused broth with carrots and turnip until tender.
why_it_fits: A long, gentle braise mirrors the pace you need when anxious — nothing to rush, just a slow return to calm.
steps: Steep chamomile in warm stock, remove bags.
Sear chicken thighs, then braise with vegetables and chamomile stock at 160°C for 70 minutes.

title: Herb-Roasted Whole Chicken with Stuffing
description: A whole chicken roasted with garlic and herbs, served with a savoury bread stuffing.
why_it_fits: A full roast dinner is the kind of meal that restores energy for the whole evening, not just the next hour.
steps: Rub chicken with butter and herbs, roast at 190°C for 75 minutes.
Sauté onion and celery, mix with bread cubes and thyme, bake stuffing alongside for the last 25 minutes.

title: Homemade Beef Lasagna
description: Layers of pasta, seasoned beef ragu, and melted mozzarella baked until bubbling.
why_it_fits: A crowd-pleasing bake worth the effort — a great mood deserves a meal that feels like a celebration.
steps: Brown beef with tomatoes for a ragu.
Layer with pasta sheets, ricotta, and mozzarella.
Bake at 190°C for 45 minutes until golden and bubbling.

title: Homemade Chicken Pot Pie
description: A buttery, flaky crust over a creamy chicken and vegetable filling, baked until golden.
why_it_fits: Rich, buttery comfort food that rewards the wait — a warm, familiar dish to come home to.
steps: Simmer chicken and vegetables in stock and cream until thickened.
Pour into a dish, top with pastry, and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes.

title: Slow-Braised Lamb Shank with Root Vegetables
description: Lamb shank braised for hours until fall-off-the-bone tender, with carrots, parsnip, and pearl onions.
why_it_fits: A slow, unhurried braise is its own kind of stress relief — there is nothing to rush, just time doing the work.
steps: Sear lamb shanks on all sides.
Add vegetables, stock, and rosemary.
Cover and braise at 160°C for 2.5 hours until tender.

title: Slow-Cooker Beef Stew
description: Chunks of beef, potato, and carrot simmered low and slow into a thick, hearty stew.
why_it_fits: A stew that takes all afternoon is a small act of caring for yourself — something warm waiting at the end of a hard day.
image_credit: A Healthier Michigan / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0
steps: Sear beef, then combine with vegetables, stock, tomato paste, and bay leaf.
Simmer on low for 3 hours until beef is fork-tender.

title: Slow-Roasted Beef Brisket with Roasted Carrots
description: Beef brisket rubbed with spices and slow-roasted for hours until tender enough to shred.
why_it_fits: A long, undistracted cook mirrors the focus you are looking to rebuild — one slow task instead of many scattered ones.
steps: Rub brisket with spices and garlic.
Roast covered at 150°C with stock and carrots for 3 hours until fork-tender, then rest before slicing.

title: Slow-Simmered Turkey Chili
description: Ground turkey simmered for over an hour with beans, tomatoes, and warming spices.
why_it_fits: A chili that simmers for an hour gives restless energy somewhere useful to go while the smell fills the kitchen.
image_credit: cyclonebill from Copenhagen / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0
steps: Brown turkey with onion, add beans, tomatoes, and spices.
Simmer uncovered for 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.

title: Walnut-Crusted Baked Salmon with Roasted Vegetables
description: Salmon fillet under a crunchy walnut crust, baked alongside roasted seasonal vegetables.
why_it_fits: Omega-3s from salmon and walnuts are two of the best-studied nutrients for sustained mental clarity.
steps: Crush walnuts with breadcrumbs and honey, press onto salmon.
Roast salmon and vegetables together at 200°C for 45 minutes until the crust is golden.

title: Whole Roasted Chicken with Lemon and Herbs
description: A golden roasted chicken stuffed with lemon and fresh herbs, served with pan juices.
why_it_fits: A bright, golden roast matches a bright mood, and it is the kind of dish worth savouring slowly.
steps: Stuff chicken cavity with lemon, garlic, and rosemary.
Rub skin with olive oil, roast at 200°C for 80 minutes with potatoes around it, basting halfway.
